target_customer: Global fintechs, wallets and businesses that need to collect, convert and settle money between African local currencies and USD or stablecoins
problem: Moving money into and out of Africa is slow and fragmented. Partna offers on and off ramp APIs that convert local currency to stablecoins and settle in USD, citing cases that went from days or months to same day.
business_model: usage-based payments API with FX and settlement spread

founders.name: Bashir Aminu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO with no biography. Not verified from an opened source.

founders.name: Hakeem Adeyemi Orewole
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a software engineer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard payments API engineering, but it needs bank rails in several African markets, FX liquidity and stablecoin conversion, which is operationally hard for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Value comes from local banking relationships and licences. The API layer itself can be copied, and other crypto on and off ramps served the same markets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A later source notes Flutterwave added stablecoin payments in October 2025 on top of its fiat business. No evidence of a direct copy of Partna found.

market_need_then: Cross-border payments into Africa were costly and slow, and stablecoin rails were a growing alternative by 2021 and 2022. The company cites customers such as MiniPay, Cenoa and HyperVerge, but those are later claims.

identity.voice_and_tone: Engineer to engineer, reliability focused: built by engineers tired of broken payment rails.

rebrands.why: Reason not stated. Sources say the company was formerly Payourse; the date is not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself. Known mainly through infrastructure partnerships and the YC listing.

outcome_analysis: Partna is still active and focuses on B2B stablecoin rails between Africa and global markets. It raised a small pre-seed as Payourse in December 2021 and went through YC in Winter 2022. Public funding after YC is not confirmed, so its trajectory is unclear. The company claims 200,000 monthly transactions and well known wallet customers, which suggests real usage, but these are unverified self reported numbers.
notes: Funding totals conflict across aggregators ($1.1M, $1.4M). The $600k pre-seed was reported by TechCabal (December 2021, title seen in search, page blocked with 403) and Seedtable. Competitors empty because no source dated near January 2022 naming rivals was found; a search returned only later Yellow Card coverage. Other profiles name a third co-founder, John Anisere, and give Aminu prior employers, but the sources were not opened so they are not recorded.
